subject.title: Unhandled socket error in SSRF fetch wrapper can kill the gateway process (IPv6-only DNS + Happy Eyeballs)

question: Should the linked SSRF socket-error fix proceed as a repaired shared dispatcher change with live/log proof, or should it be folded into the broader guarded-fetch family-policy work?
rationale: The bug is valid, but the implementation path crosses the SSRF security boundary and the current linked PR has already shown proxy/pinning contract risk, so automation should not choose the permanent security-boundary shape alone.

options.title: Repair linked shared fix
options.body: Keep this issue open, require the linked PR or replacement to preserve pinned lookup and proxy `requestTls` contracts, and ask for IPv6-unreachable proof before merge.

options.title: Fold into broader family-policy tracker
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87763 as the design umbrella if maintainers want one larger guarded-fetch address-family repair instead of a narrow crash fix.

options.title: Wait for live repro first
options.body: Pause the fix path until a maintainer or contributor captures a current-main Docker/Linux reproduction, accepting the known availability risk meanwhile.

recommendation.title: Repair linked shared fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, require the linked PR or replacement to preserve pinned lookup and proxy `requestTls` contracts, and ask for IPv6-unreachable proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history in the central SSRF dispatcher and explicit-proxy pinning paths that constrain the fix shape.
